reviewer: local Codex reviewer; not GPT Plus #2

findings.title: R6 input and R5 predecessor hashes do not bind raw committed bytes
findings.summary: R6 declares 29 inputs but only 22 match raw committed bytes. Six mismatches become exact under LF-to-CRLF normalization. One FINISH-08 diagnostic test differs by one inserted CR byte at offset 2872. The R5 output manifest and 23 of its 32 outputs also fail raw-byte comparisons, but all those outputs are documentation/evidence and become exact after LF-to-CRLF normalization; all six R5 source replacements are exact.

singleByteException.difference: one inserted CR byte 0x0d at offset 2872

r5PredecessorManifest.mismatchedOutputScope: documentation/evidence only; no source replacement mismatch

internalIdentityConflict.relationship: source-build identity matches the committed LF blob; input-hashes expectation matches CRLF conversion

findings.impact: Raw-byte provenance for inherited R5 inputs cannot be established from the candidate input/output manifests without a declared canonicalization rule. Independent assembly, tests and browser checks support the source behavior and all current source replacements are exact; this finding is about reproducibility and evidence identity, not a demonstrated runtime defect.
findings.reproduction: Run the pinned candidate hash verification and inspect the declared input and predecessor output comparison rows in evidence/candidate-hash-receipt.json. Run python .work/analyze-eol-fin16.py and python .work/analyze-single-byte-fin16.py; outputs are preserved under evidence/logs.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate or explicitly canonicalize inherited input/output hash receipts against committed Git blobs, document the byte representation being hashed, and rerun verification. Do not infer a source fix from this finding.

limitations: Local Codex reviewer only; designated external GPT Plus #2 review is not claimed.
Historical R5 red invocation was NOT RUN because its command was not retained and FINISH-16 says not to rewrite R5.
Provider/CDN, deployment, physical/manual-device, accessibility/assistive-technology, and G7 acceptance were NOT RUN.
The optional rollback browser fault throws at second-target assignment before that target mutates; the first target was changed and then rolled back.
